notable_absence.finding: The page states a hard constraint with no named enforcement mechanism: 'your synonym documents and collections must not be included as fields in your Search index definition' - but never says what happens if they ARE included (a build error, silently wrong results, or something else), and no predicate in the registry cleanly captures a 'must be excluded from a definition' shape (doesNotSupport is about a feature not working with something, not about a required exclusion of input data) - flagged rather than force-fit.

cross_component_finding: This page's thesaurus/synonym-collection language ('a thesaurus is divided into synonym collections that contain synonym documents') is the first page in this batch to name the FULL containment chain explicitly: thesaurus > synonym collection > synonym document, with 'synonym source' (search:synonym-source, already extraction-layer) as the fourth, index-level naming layer that POINTS INTO a synonym collection rather than containing it. Four names, four distinct roles, and no single page in this batch states all four in one place - add-synonym-source.md and its Quick sibling describe the source-to-field wiring, create-synonym-collection-docs.md and its sibling describe the collection/document creation, and only this page names the aggregate thesaurus. Also notable: this page and synonyms-search-quick.json (this same batch) are near-identical in body text in exactly the same way the create-synonym-collection-docs pair is (see that record's finding) - but a concurrent sibling batch this round already split THIS pair into two ids (search:synonyms-search / search:synonyms-search-quick) before this batch could apply its own one-id convention; see synonyms-search-quick.json for the full writeup of that tension.
